summaryZh: TREJOLab 研究控制血管炎症与乳腺癌进展的细胞信号通路，涉及 G 蛋白偶联受体、ARRDC3 及泛素驱动的炎症信号。成员页列明 Gilsuk Yang 的研究工作为 GPCR 单粒子追踪。
researchQuestions: 细胞信号如何控制血管炎症和癌症？
GPCR 泛素化触发的 p38 炎症信号通路如何受到调控？
GPCR 如何以及为何进入依赖 ALIX 和 ARRDC3 的溶酶体分选通路？
methods: GPCR单粒子追踪（成员Gilsuk Yang所列研究工作）

evidence.quote: TREJOLab Cell signaling in health and disease
Our research is focused on understanding the cell signaling pathways that control vascular inflammation and breast cancer progression.
We study the function of G protein-coupled receptors, specifically protease-activated receptors, the tumor suppressor alpha-arrestin ARRDC3 and ubiquitin-driven inflammatory signaling.
The TREJOLab is located in the School of Medicine on the UC San Diego Health Sciences campus in La Jolla, CA.
Our research is focused on cell signaling and how it controls vascular inflammation and cancer.
We discovered that ubiquitination of a subset of GPCRs initiates p38 inflammatory signaling and endothelial dysfunction. A major challenge is to understand how this pathway is regulated.

Another challenge is to understand how and why GPCRs sort into the ALIX and ARRDC3- dependent lysosomal sorting pathway and the impact of the tumor suppressor ARRDC3 on GPCR signaling and cancer progression.
Scientist, single particle tracking of GPCRs Gilsuk Yang, PhD Postdoctoral Scholar
